title.analysis: Authentic title "Why Everything Changes After You Start Looking Poor" reuses the channel's "Why Everything Changes After..." threshold frame. The script delivers stealth-wealth (Stanley-Danko, lifestyle creep, lottery-neighbour bankruptcies, redirecting car payments), then flips to the poverty premium (payday, subprime, insurance) and quiet luxury. It answers the title in both directions. TYPICAL against the cohort. Association only.

script.opening_words: The broke one is driving the nicer car. Watch what happens at this red light. In the front, Peter is drumming the wheel of a leased German sedan, chrome rims, a watch that cost $1,100, and a 900 a month payment he doesn't say out loud. Four cars back, Lara is sipping from a dented thermos in a 2014 Camry with 190,000 mi and a coffee stain on the passenger seat that has outlived two of her phones. You glance
script.ending_words: it looks like from the outside when you finally have nothing left to prove. So, drive the boring car, wear the cheap watch, let them underestimate you all the way to the bank. And if you want the actual playbook, the boring, beautiful math that turns a Peter into a Lyra, you already know where the door is. That's what our school community is for. I'll see you in there.
script.analysis: Full 19494 canonical characters read. A single-narrator essay with composites: red-light hook (leased sedan vs old Camry); channel pitch and an open loop on the lottery study; Stanley-Danko millionaire habits; Experian luxury-car ownership; Goldman paycheck-to-paycheck at $300-500K; Diderot effect and hedonic adaptation; car payments, 84-month loans, negative equity; dealer payment framing; BNPL for burritos, Coachella and groceries; Fed lottery-neighbour bankruptcy study; redirected $700 payment to ~$850K; savings rate and early start; Buffett and Kamprad; paid community plug; poverty premium (payday, subprime, rent-to-own, insurance); Veblen; dress-based service; underconsumption, loud budgeting, money dysmorphia; quiet luxury; objection about appearances; close and community plug. Reproduces: $700 x 30 years at 7%/8%; 30-vs-35-year gap. Mostly accurate references. Caveats: Toyota statistic from a later Stanley book; Experian figures dated; auto figures slightly behind the latest Edmunds quarter; rent-to-own example exceeds the stated multiple. The stored ending is complete.

topic.analysis: Stealth wealth versus performed wealth: how visible consumption drains finances, the math of redirecting car payments, and the opposite poverty premium charged to people who look risky.
topic.audience_problem: Earners tempted to signal success through cars and goods while falling behind.
topic.time_sensitivity: Low-medium: evergreen thesis with dated auto and BNPL statistics.
topic.narrative_angle: Looking poor is freedom if you are secure, and a tax if you are not.
topic.novelty_and_corpus_angle: Test stealth-wealth narratives that pair the frugality story with its counterpoint (the poverty premium). Cite each study's year and population on screen, and update auto statistics to the latest quarter.
